We introduce a model of multiple-body superconductivity within topological flat bands, where the superconducting order parameter is defined by a many-body wave function. This approach allows for the analysis of the system's ground state and its topological characteristics. We demonstrate that the model supports a topological superconducting phase featuring a non-trivial Chern number, which is accompanied by a quantized thermal Hall effect.
This paper establishes a universal version of Polya's theorem for locally compact Abelian groups of dimension 1.

This study evaluates the performance of several clustering techniques on high-dimensional presence-absence datasets. We examine the efficacy of the k-means algorithm, hierarchical clustering, and the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) when applied to data with a binary structure. Our findings indicate that the GMM outperforms the other methods in this specific context.

Salient object detection (SOD) aims to identify the most visually prominent regions within an image. While numerous methods have been developed, they often rely on specific cues, such as color or depth, which can limit their effectiveness. This paper introduces a unified framework that integrates both RGB and RGB-D data to enhance SOD performance. The proposed approach employs a multi-scale feature extraction module to capture salient information from both modalities, followed by a multi-scale feature fusion module that combines these features. Finally, a multi-scale feature aggregation module is used to generate the final saliency map. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper outlines the approach taken by the University of Michigan and Indiana University team for the SemEval-2019 Challenge 6, which focused on detecting aggression in tweets. Our methodology involved training a BERT model on a dataset of 10,000 tweets, followed by the development of a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. This classifier was trained on a subset of 1,000 tweets and subsequently applied to the test set. Our final submission achieved a score of 0.800, ranking 10th out of 100 participants.
This paper examines the quotients of symmetrical and antisymmetrical numbers, specifically focusing on the properties of their remainders.

This study introduces a non-convex variational framework designed to simultaneously address polyenergetic computed tomography (CT) reconstruction, sensor noise reduction, and material decomposition. The proposed approach employs a non-convex regularization term to enhance the quality of the reconstructed images. The resulting optimization problem is solved using an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses noise and improves the quality of the reconstructed images.

This study introduces a novel method for generating synthetic handwritten text images, designed to enhance the performance of low-resource handwritten text recognition (HTR) systems. The proposed approach employs a single-shot technique that utilizes a single source image to create a diverse set of synthetic samples. By applying a series of transformations, the method generates variations in font, size, and style, while also introducing realistic noise and distortions. The resulting synthetic data is then used to train a deep learning model for HTR. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly improves the performance of low-resource HTR systems, particularly when the available training data is scarce.

This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the ground-state properties of heavy nuclei, specifically focusing on the $^{208}\text{Pb}$ and $^{209}\text{Bi}$ isotopes. The investigation employs a relativistic mean-field framework to calculate the single-particle energy levels and the corresponding nuclear density distributions. The results are then compared against experimental data and findings from other theoretical models.

This study examines the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, a paradigmatic example of a topological insulator, to explore the fundamental concepts of topological quantum phenomena. We analyze the model's Hamiltonian and its associated topological invariant, the winding number, to demonstrate how this quantity predicts the existence of edge states. Furthermore, we investigate the influence of disorder on the system, showing that while it can disrupt the topological phase, it also enables the emergence of localized states within the bulk.

This paper investigates the compactness of composition operators acting on Bergman spaces over convex domains and analytic disks. We establish that a composition operator is compact if and only if the associated symbol is a proper map.

This paper introduces DynaSOAr, a concurrent memory allocator designed for object-oriented development on GPUs. It addresses the limitations of existing GPU allocators, which are often restricted to C/C++ and lack support for object-oriented features. DynaSOAr offers a novel approach to memory allocation that is both efficient and effective, enabling the creation of complex object-oriented applications on GPUs.

This study examines the mechanical behavior of a pressurized straw conduit, focusing on the longitudinal stress distribution and the resulting mechanical integrity. The analysis employs a theoretical framework based on the thin-walled pressure vessel model, which is validated against experimental data. The findings indicate that the longitudinal stress is directly proportional to the internal pressure and the conduit's radius, while being inversely proportional to its wall thickness. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the conduit's mechanical integrity is significantly influenced by the magnitude of the internal pressure, the conduit's radius, and the wall thickness.

This paper introduces a novel framework for credal Bayesian inference that leverages probabilistic circuits to represent credal sets. By utilizing these circuits, we establish a method for computing lower and upper bounds on the posterior probability of any query. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the framework can be adapted to enforce constraints on the posterior distribution, thereby enabling the derivation of rigorous strength guarantees for the resulting inference.

We introduce a novel mechanism for Bloch oscillations within a superfluid, driven by a spatially periodic potential that varies in time. This setup creates a dynamic energy gap, which we demonstrate can be closed by tuning the potential's frequency. We further show that this gap closure enables the superfluid to undergo Bloch oscillations.

This paper introduces a novel class of codes, termed neighbor-transitive codes, which are defined by a specific property of their associated partial dispersions. We demonstrate that these codes are equivalent to the partial dispersions of neighbor-transitive generalized quadrangles. Furthermore, we establish that the codes derived from the partial dispersions of the classical generalized quadrangles are precisely the neighbor-transitive codes.

The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of the Milky Way is a dense, anisotropic region of gas and stars. This study introduces a novel method to quantify the anisotropic mass distribution within the CMZ by analyzing the two-dimensional correlation function of the gas. We applied this technique to the 12CO(1-0) emission data from the CMZ, revealing that the gas mass distribution is highly anisotropic, with a preferred orientation aligned along the Galactic plane.

This study introduces a rate framework for modeling electron populations in non-linear high-fluence X-ray absorption edge spectra. The model accounts for the interplay between the photoelectric effect, Auger decay, and the subsequent relaxation of excited states. By applying this framework to the K-edge of copper, we demonstrate that the model accurately reproduces the observed non-linear behavior.

This paper introduces a compact temperature detector capable of operating across a 0.6V to 1.8V supply range, featuring a 0.24°C resolution and a ±1.4°C accuracy. The device achieves a power consumption of 1.06nJ per conversion, with a total area of 0.0025mm².

We present a method for generating polarization-entangled photon pairs using quantum scissors, a technique that relies on the probabilistic splitting of single photons. This approach is particularly advantageous for quantum communication protocols, as it enables the creation of entangled states with a high degree of purity.

This paper introduces a novel class of geometric structures termed virtual Euclidean spanners, which are defined as a pair consisting of a graph and a mapping from its edges to the Euclidean plane. We establish that for any given graph, a virtual Euclidean spanner can be constructed with a stretch factor of $O(1)$ and a size of $O(n \log n)$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for any graph, a virtual Euclidean spanner with a stretch factor of $O(1)$ and a size of $O(n)$ can be achieved.

This study introduces a novel approach to classifying IoT devices by leveraging their feature sets. The proposed method employs a cost-conscious feature extraction technique that prioritizes the most informative features while minimizing computational expenses. The resulting feature set is then utilized to train a machine learning model for device classification. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through experiments on a dataset comprising 1,000 IoT devices, where the results indicate that the proposed approach achieves superior classification accuracy compared to existing methods.

This paper investigates the algebraic and relational semantics of G\"{o}del modal logic and its extensions. We demonstrate that the algebraic semantics for these systems are generated by the algebras of G\"{o}del-H\"{o}fer logic, which are themselves derived from the algebras of G\"{o}del logic. Furthermore, we establish that the relational semantics for these systems are generated by the relational structures of G\"{o}del logic.

This study introduces a novel method for aligning words in parallel corpora by leveraging external bilingual resources. The approach employs a probabilistic model that integrates word alignment probabilities derived from a bilingual dictionary with those from a standard statistical model. We demonstrate that this technique significantly enhances alignment quality, particularly when applied to low-resource language pairs.

This paper introduces a novel approach to constructing Nash equilibria in games with continuous strategy spaces, utilizing a distorted resolvent method. The method is demonstrated to be effective for games featuring a continuous action set and a continuous payoff function.

We present a simulation of a universe containing primordial black holes (PBHs) that serve as dark energy, utilizing the PopSyCLE code. This study examines the evolution of PBHs across a range of initial masses and formation redshifts, with a specific focus on the PBHs' impact on the cosmic expansion history.

We examine a system of rigid wedges made of balls, where the wedges are arranged in a splay configuration. This setup is analyzed using a continuum model that incorporates a splay term. The study demonstrates that the system's energy is bounded from below and that the associated minimization problem is solvable. Furthermore, the existence of a splay-modulated stage is established, and the asymptotic behavior of the energy is determined.

This study introduces a novel class of one-step recurrences for static random fields defined on the sphere, which are derived from the recurrence relations of the associated random walks. We establish that these recurrences are valid for any static random field on the sphere, provided the field's covariance function is a positive definite function on the sphere. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the resulting one-step recurrences are equivalent to the Karhunen-Loève expansion.

We introduce a single-pixel quantum imaging method that does not require particle detection, relying instead on the interference of undetected particles. This approach utilizes a single-pixel detector to measure the interference pattern of a probe beam, which is modulated by the presence of an object. The resulting image is reconstructed by applying a Fourier transform to the recorded interference data.

We introduce a model for liquid foams that incorporates a texture-dependent friction mechanism. This framework is applied to analyze the dynamics of a foam layer situated on a moving substrate. The study reveals that the foam's texture significantly influences the frictional forces, which in turn dictate the foam's behavior.

This study introduces a novel deep learning framework for identifying skin cancer, designed to enhance the accuracy of skin lesion classification. The proposed method employs a two-stage approach: first, it utilizes a deep learning model to classify lesions, and second, it applies an entropy-based technique to detect outlier samples. The efficacy of this method was evaluated using the ISIC 2018 dataset, demonstrating that the entropy-based outlier detection significantly improves classification performance.

We present a study of the quasi-particle lifetime in sodium, an almost-free electron metal, utilizing angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). By analyzing the spectral function, we observe that the quasi-particle lifetime is governed by electron-electron scattering, which aligns with the predictions of Fermi liquid theory.

This study introduces a novel method for addressing the phase space volume variation problem, which is a significant challenge in the field of molecular dynamics. The proposed approach utilizes Hamiltonian paths to achieve this goal. The paper also provides a detailed analysis of the free expansion process, which serves as a primary example of the method's application.
This paper presents a method for computing the Kontsevich weights of link and curvature graphs within the framework of symplectic Poisson structures.

This study examines the existence of nanoptera within a nonlinear woodpile structure and a diatomic granular array, both of which are weakly nonlinear. We demonstrate that these systems support nanoptera, which are solitary waves characterized by exponentially decaying oscillations. Furthermore, we establish that the amplitude of these waves is governed by a specific nonlinear dispersion relation.

We examine the cosmological collider framework, which utilizes primordial fluctuations to probe the physics of heavy particles present during inflation. We demonstrate that the standard cosmological collider approach is a specific instance of a broader methodology, which we term "primal features." This generalized framework encompasses the traditional collider method and extends to other scenarios, such as the detection of heavy particles in the early universe via the imprint of their signatures on the primordial power spectrum.

This paper introduces a novel class of graphs termed accordion charts, which are quartic and circulant. We establish a graph-theoretic framework for this problem and demonstrate that the leakage can be quantified using the graph's fractional chromatic number. Furthermore, we derive a lower bound for the leakage in terms of the graph's fractional clique number.

This study introduces a novel hierarchical deep generative model for super-resolving synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, termed MrSARP. The architecture employs a multi-scale approach to progressively refine low-resolution inputs into high-resolution outputs. Specifically, the model utilizes a multi-scale encoder to extract features from the input, a multi-scale decoder to reconstruct the image, and a multi-scale generator to produce the final high-resolution result. The proposed method is evaluated on both simulated and real-world SAR datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is a variational quantum method designed to tackle combinatorial optimization problems. This study introduces a Bayesian approach to optimize QAOA parameters, utilizing a Gaussian process to model the cost function and a Bayesian optimization strategy to identify the optimal settings. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through numerical experiments on the MaxCut problem, showing that it surpasses standard random search techniques.

The approach relies on a specific property of the intersection points: they are the roots of a quartic equation. The method involves constructing this quartic equation and then solving it to identify the intersection points.

We investigate the magnetic properties of the extended Hubbard model on a triangular lattice using a combination of mean-field theory and the random-phase approximation. Our findings reveal that the system exhibits a rich phase diagram, featuring a variety of magnetic states, including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and stripe configurations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the ground state of the system is determined by the interplay between quantum fluctuations and thermal effects, leading to an order-by-disorder mechanism.

This study introduces a novel framework for the automated localization and recognition of vertebrae in CT scans, utilizing a spine rectification technique to enhance the performance of a deep learning-based segmentation model. The proposed method first employs a deep learning network to identify the spine's centerline, followed by a rectification process that aligns the spine to a standard orientation. Subsequently, a deep learning model performs segmentation on the rectified spine, and the resulting labels are mapped back to the original image. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves superior performance compared to existing methods, with a Dice coefficient of 0.935 and a Hausdorff distance of 2.01 mm.

This paper introduces a novel framework for random thermodynamics, which is a generalization of the classical theory of random currents. We establish that the asymptotic data of this theory is gauge invariant.

We introduce a relative quantum topology for smooth projective varieties, which is defined by the birational equivalence class of their quantum cohomology rings. This framework is applied to demonstrate that the quantum cohomology rings of the blow-ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $n$ points are pairwise non-isomorphic for any $n \geq 1$.

This study examines the transmission of acoustic waves between two piezoelectric crystals positioned in close proximity. The analysis demonstrates that the transmission coefficient can reach unity, indicating complete wave transfer, when the crystals are separated by a specific distance. This phenomenon is explained by the formation of a standing wave within the gap between the crystals.

We introduce a reservoir optical model for exciton-polariton aggregates, which are formed by the interaction between excitons and photons within a microcavity. This model is derived from a microscopic Hamiltonian that accounts for the coupling between excitons and photons, as well as the exciton-exciton interaction. We demonstrate that the model accurately reproduces the dynamics of the exciton-polariton system, including the emergence of a reservoir of excitons. Furthermore, we show that the model can be used to investigate the effects of exciton-exciton interactions on the exciton-polariton system.

We present the first detection of a dust disk around the exoplanet K2-22 b, a massive, hot Jupiter located 120 parsecs away. Utilizing the Large Binocular Telescope's Integral Field Unit, we identified a 1.2-micron emission feature, which we attribute to the presence of large dust grains. Our findings indicate that the planet's mass loss rate is approximately 100 times higher than that of the Sun, a phenomenon likely driven by the planet's proximity to its host star.
This paper establishes that the Milnor fiber of a holomorphic function is coherent if and only if the critical set of the function is flat.

This paper introduces Daany, a .NET-based data analytics framework designed to facilitate the analysis of large-scale datasets. The system is built upon the .NET Core platform and leverages the Apache Spark engine to execute distributed computations. The authors present a comprehensive overview of the framework's architecture and provide a detailed examination of its core components.

This paper examines the relationship between mathematics and philosophy during the Scientific Revolution, specifically analyzing Galileo's *Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems*. It argues that Galileo's work was not merely a philosophical treatise but a mathematical one, as he employed mathematical reasoning to demonstrate the superiority of the Copernican system over the Ptolemaic one.

We examine the non-Gaussian signatures of the Saha ionization epoch within the early universe, focusing on the primordial power spectrum and the bispectrum. Our analysis indicates that the Saha ionization epoch generates a non-Gaussian signal in the bispectrum that is significantly stronger than that produced by the standard inflationary model.

This study employs a hybrid magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and particle-in-cell (PIC) model to investigate the merging of magnetic islands in a tokamak plasma. The simulation utilizes a 2D MHD framework for the background plasma, while the PIC method is applied to a localized region to capture kinetic effects. The results demonstrate that the merging process is significantly influenced by the kinetic behavior of electrons, which is accurately represented by the embedded PIC model.

This paper introduces Scribe, a novel approach to teaching programming that leverages a generative model to create a personalized, interactive learning environment. The system analyzes a student's code to generate a tailored set of exercises, which are then presented to the student in a conversational format. The study evaluates Scribe's effectiveness by comparing it against a standard curriculum, demonstrating that the proposed method significantly enhances student performance.
